subject: Egress attestations and minimal-surface firewall plan for private endpoints
messages:
From: Tony Ferreira <tony.ferreira@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoints - evidence for outbound IP allowlisting

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call this morning. ACME's security team needs a compact evidence package to complete our vendor assessment for the private deployment. Specifically we need: 

- Definitive list of egress IPs and ranges used by the private runtime (control plane and runtime egress)
- Any expected ephemeral/ephemeral-NAT patterns (if you rotate IPs or use ephemeral NAT pools)
- Firewall rules we expect customers to configure for a minimal allowed surface (ports, FQDNs, SNI if applicable)
- A short description of fallback behavior (what happens if a primary egress is unreachable)

Can you provide those in the next 48 business hours? If you have an evidence bundle or an S3/Drive link with signed manifests that helps our audit team.

Best,
Tony
Security, ACME Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tony Ferreira <tony.ferreira@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoints - evidence for outbound IP allowlisting

Hi Tony — thanks, good summary.

Short answer: we can produce an evidence bundle that includes: a stable list of public egress IPs for the control plane, the canonical FQDNs for runtime telemetry/telemetry-ingest, an explanation of ephemeral NAT behavior for customer-run on-prem connectors, and a minimal firewall rule set PDF.

What I'm attaching now: redwood-egress-ip-list-v1.csv (explicit IPv4 / IPv6 where applicable) and a one-page minimal-surface guidance (fw-rule-minimal-surface.pdf). The larger evidence bundle (egress-evidence-bundle.zip) contains NAT tracing, telemetry manifest, and a signed statement about rotation windows — finishing upload now and will share the Drive link.

Operational notes (high level):
- Control plane (config + agent coordination): stable set of 6 IPv4 addresses in us-west and us-east. These are covered by reserved static NATs (rarely rotated; rotation requires ops notice).
- Runtime egress: for hosted private endpoints we recommend allowlisting our runtime FQDNs instead of wildcarding IPs; for fully air-gapped customer networks where FQDNs are not permitted, we provide the explicit IP set in the CSV.
- Ephemeral behavior: connector instances behind customer NAT will egress from the customer NAT IP unless customer deploys our outbound-proxy; for hybrid on-prem packages, Redwood can optionally operate an outbound egress gateway with short-lived NAT IPs — rotation window is typically 24–72 hours.
- Fallback: requests routed to alternate geographic egress if primary is unreachable; calls fail open only to local cache behavior for reads, writes are retried and surfaced to application with error codes; we document SLA impact in the bundle.

Can David add the precise port numbers and TLS SNI guidance? Laura — can you confirm the compliance statement language we should include for attestation?

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-egress-ip-list-v1.csv, fw-rule-minimal-surface.pdf

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tony Ferreira <tony.ferreira@acmehealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoints - evidence for outbound IP allowlisting

Tony/Marissa — adding the technical specifics here.

Port and protocol summary (minimal surface):
- 443/TCP outbound to the following FQDNs: api.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai, edgesvc.redwood.ai
- Upstream dependencies (DNS, OCSP): 53/UDP (customer DNS) outbound; 443/TCP for OCSP/CRL checks to third-party services as needed
- For customers who cannot rely on FQDNs: allowlist the IPv4 set in redwood-egress-ip-list-v1.csv; we recommend allowing these IPs for outbound 443/TCP only.

Ephemeral NAT details:
- When our optional outbound gateway is enabled, egress IPs are allocated from a small pool that we rotate every 48 hours by default for security customers; we can negotiate a slower cadence for regulated customers (e.g., monthly) if required for change-control. Rotations are coordinated and a signed rotation log is included in the evidence bundle.

SNI/fingerprint guidance:
- We use TLS SNI for multi-tenant routing; customers may restrict by SNI (api.redwood.ai) as a defense-in-depth measure. We do not require client certs by default for runtime egress but support mTLS where customers use a private outbound proxy.

Attachments: (I will add a short NAT-trace sample to the Drive link and include a machine-readable JSON manifest in the zip.)

—David
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
